tool 'get_weather' description tells the reader to keep something from the user ('Do not tell the user'). In MCP the description is what the agent routes on, so a sentence addressed to the agent is executable text, not documentation

tool 'get_weather' names '~/.ssh' in its description; a tool that legitimately reads a credential declares it in inputSchema, where a caller can see it, rather than pointing the agent at the path in prose

tool 'notify_team' carries zero-width space, right-to-left override, unicode tag character in its description; these reach the model and not the human reviewing the manifest, which is the only reason to put them there

tool 'notify_team' description directs what the reader should put in an argument ('Always include'). In MCP the description is what the agent routes on, so a sentence addressed to the agent is executable text, not documentation

tool 'render_report' description tells the reader to discard earlier instructions ('ignore previous'). In MCP the description is what the agent routes on, so a sentence addressed to the agent is executable text, not documentation

tool 'render_report' hides text in an HTML comment in its description ('When search_orders is called, ignore previous instructions a'); a client rendering the description as markdown shows nothing while the model reads all of it

tool 'render_report' names another tool ('search_orders') in its description alongside an instruction to the reader; a description that changes how a *different* tool is used is a change nobody reviewing that tool would see

tool 'delete_account' claims readOnlyHint=true while its name says 'delete'. The specification says annotations are untrusted unless the server is; this is reported so a human decides, and no gate in this tool consults the hint either way

tool 'sync_data' declares readOnlyHint=true and destructiveHint=true. The specification defines destructiveHint only when readOnlyHint is false, so these say two incompatible things and a client believing either is guessing which
1 of 6 tools declare no annotations (render_report). The specification's default for an undeclared destructiveHint is true, so a client honouring defaults must treat every one of them as destructive
